endorsements.quote: Alongside preference, relevant outcomes would include objective comprehension, rec ognition of uncertainty, recall of follow-up recommendations, emotional response, and intended action.
Patient participants could reflect a range of cancer stages, ages, educational backgrounds, primary languages, and health-literacy levels.

unlisted_practices: Evaluate AI-generated patient-facing explanations within their intended clinical pathway, including clear labelling, access to clinician-verified information, and a route for clarification when findings are urgent or uncertain.
Evaluate AI report simplification on unselected consecutive reports so that difficult cases are retained, and classify errors by likely clinical consequence rather than only an overall rating.
Use mixed-effects models with reader and case effects to account for crossed ratings in adequately powered validation studies of AI-generated reports.

screen.reason: This is a letter to the editor/commentary discussing the limitations of a prior study on AI-simplified oncology imaging reports and recommending future research directions and validation practices for patient-facing LLM outputs.
